messages:
maria: customer reported embeddings throughput regression after last rollout. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec drops ~65%. seeing intermittent dimension-mismatch warnings and a couple of 502s. customer says "vectors per sec": 12 -> 4"

dan: can you paste a sample request id and exact timestamps? is this limited to one customer/model?

maria: request ids: req-acme-3a2f (13:02:11 UTC), req-acme-3a9b (13:07:44 UTC). model pinned to into-embed-1536-q8_a. customer asserts batch sizes unchanged. logs attached (short excerpt below).

maria: ```
2026-03-15T13:02:11Z req-acme-3a2f embeddings start model=into-embed-1536-q8_a batch=8
2026-03-15T13:02:11Z kv_cache: hit ratio=0.12
2026-03-15T13:02:11Z gpu: queue_depth=24, active_streams=8, mem_free=18GB
2026-03-15T13:02:11Z embeddings: returned_dim=0 warning=dim-mismatch
2026-03-15T13:02:12Z req-acme-3a2f 502 upstream_error
```

sanjay: interesting — returned_dim=0 usually means a serialization or fallback path produced a sparse/empty vector. 502 could be upstream model crash or runtime OOM. queue_depth=24 + active_streams=8 suggests GPU queueing but not full saturation yet. did we change batch window or autoscale?

maria: we rolled a tiny batching tweak yesterday (window lowered from 12ms -> 8ms) to reduce latency. rollout annotated in deploy bot: @ops-bot deployed into-embed-1536-q8_a to region-us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T02:00Z :rocket:

ops-bot: Deploy complete: into-embed-1536-q8_a v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0. Canary 100% at 2026-03-15T02:00Z.

d an: (typo) dan: The batching change could increase batch count variance and reduce effective tokens->vectors batching efficiency. If batches shrink, CPU/GPU kernel throughput drops. Also check kernel selection logs (we pick int8 kernels for q8_a). Can you collect a three-minute trace around 13:02?

maria: grabbing trace now. Also customer sent curl that triggers reproduction:

maria: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"model":"into-embed-1536-q8_a","input":["lorem ipsum"],"batch":8}' | jq .
```

alice: I queried infra metrics for that timeframe. GPU util climbs to ~62% but GPU queue length spikes to 30-40 at 13:02. Host-level throttling appeared on node rwd-embed-03 (throttled due to high kernel context-switches). Network retransmits low. No node OOMs in that window.

sanjay: Kernel context-switches can appear if too many short-lived CUDA streams are created. The batching window reduction (8ms) would cause more small batches -> more streams. That can hurt throughput and produce intermittent failures if memory accounting hits edge cases. Also the returned_dim=0 looks like our fallback serializer triggered when model output shape check failed — need to see model logs (inference process stderr).

maria: pulled inference stderr for req-acme-3a2f:

maria: ```
[2026-03-15 13:02:11.345] ERROR: model_worker: runtime exception: attention kernel failed: launch failed: out of memory? fallback to cpu-serialize -> produced empty tensor
[2026-03-15 13:02:11.346] WARNING: serializer: output shape mismatch expected (1536) got (0)
```

dan: that lines up. So plan: revert batching window tweak for canary hosts, repro with same traffic pattern, and capture kernel selection + CUDA mem stats. Also check if quantization path change in v2.8.0 touched kernel choices.

maria: I've set canary back to v2.7.1 for region-us-west-2 on two affected pools and asked customer to test. ticketing: ACME-4721. pinging customer success for communication.

ops-bot: Rollback executed: into-embed-1536-q8_a canary set to v2.7.1 on pool rwd-embed-02,rwd-embed-03 at 2026-03-15T14:00Z.

alice: post-rollback GPU queue_depth normalized to 6-8 and vectors/sec returned to baseline in the recorded window. No further 502s seen for the customer in subsequent 20m.

maria: next steps: eng-ml to audit v2.8.0 kernel selection changes and confirm quantization fallback behavior; infra to add a short-lived-stream guard and autotune batching window defaults; support to update customer and close if green.

d an: (dan): I'll open a follow-up PR to add a stream pooling heuristic and a perf test using small-batch microbenchmarks. Also will add an assertion that serializer never returns zero-dim without raising a hard error to simplify postmortem.

maria: thanks all — marking this as escalated -> resolved (pending follow-up PRs). Customer wants a short writeup and preventive change log.
